steps.title: Base plate, base actuator and electronics
steps.instructions: Press the eight M3 inserts into the base plate at 220 °C. Seat the STS3215 (ID 1) with its spline up and fix it with four M3×8. Mount the controller PCBA on M2.5 standoffs with the USB-C port facing the rear cut-out.
warnings: Set the servo to ID 1 before mounting (Morph flashes IDs in step 6).

steps.title: Turret
steps.instructions: Drop the lazy-susan bearing over the base boss, then bolt the turret shell to the J1 horn at 0° (index mark forward).

steps.title: Shoulder
steps.instructions: Fit the J2 servo into the turret cradle. Attach the upper-arm link to the horn with the arm vertical (servo at 2048 ticks).
warnings: Do not back-drive the servo by hand while powered.

steps.title: Upper arm + elbow
steps.instructions: Mount J3 at the top of the upper arm and attach the forearm link straight up. Run the bus cable along the link channel.

steps.title: Forearm + wrist
steps.instructions: Install the J4 wrist-pitch servo and the wrist link. Check ±108° of travel without cable snag.

steps.title: Bus wiring + servo IDs
steps.instructions: Daisy-chain W1-W6 from the PCBA bus port through each servo. Connect USB-C and run `morph flash ids` to assign IDs 1-6 one servo at a time.
warnings: Leave a 30 mm service loop at every joint.

steps.title: Gripper body
steps.instructions: Mount the gripper servo (ID 6) to the gripper plate, press the pinion onto its spline and slide both racks in from the sides.

steps.title: Fingers and sensor pads
steps.instructions: Seat each FSR 402 in its finger pocket (tail through the slot), slide the pad onto the dovetail, then bolt the fingers to the racks with the pads touching a 44 mm gauge.
warnings: Torque finger screws to 0.6 N·m max: the FSR reads preload.
